ideas.title: The Interactive Red Number Glitch
ideas.angle: A high-speed interactive math test that forces the brain into a predictable 'repetition loop'. The video commands the viewer to think of a number, then correctly guesses it. This triggers massive engagement as users comment if it worked for them.

hook.en: Pick a number between five and twelve.

ideas.reason: Interactive mind-reading Shorts consistently hit 100%+ APV because the viewer must wait for the reveal. The '7' result is a statistically proven cognitive bias when people are rushed.
sources: The 'Blue Hammer' effect and number selection bias studies

ideas.title: The 3-Point Eye Contact Power Play
ideas.angle: A specific micro-behavior hack showing how looking at three points on someone's face creates immediate psychological dominance or attraction. It challenges the viewer to try it on the next person they see, driving high shares and saves.

hook.en: Look at their left eye, then their mouth.

ideas.reason: Social power dynamics and 'dark' psychology tips are currently dominating the VVSA metric because they offer immediate, actionable 'real world' value.
sources: Joe Navarro, former FBI agent, on non-verbal communication patterns
Journal of Nonverbal Behavior on gaze patterns

ideas.title: The 10-Second Vision Eraser Test
ideas.angle: An interactive optical illusion where the viewer stares at a central dot until peripheral objects vanish (Troxler's Effect). This 'body glitch' forces the viewer to stay motionless for 15+ seconds, skyrocketing retention.

hook.en: Stare at the black dot and don't blink.

ideas.reason: Sensory adaptation tests have high completion rates because the 'payoff' only happens at the very end of the video, ensuring the viewer watches the full duration.
sources: Visual Neuroscience studies on peripheral fading
